phases.name: Slice-01: the spot page names what killed the day, per day section
phases.description: Plumbing plus a render, never modelling. The engine already picks the culprit and the receipt already carries it; the value simply never crosses into the file the pages read. This phase closes that carry inside src/publish, adds one self-contained component, and stops.

steps.name: Shared Spanish factor vocabulary in one movable module
criteria: One module maps each of the four factor tokens to its Spanish noun and definite article; no other Spanish factor word exists anywhere in this lane.
The module imports nothing at all, so the later move into the shared data lane is a file move plus an import path change.
Property: every factor token resolves to a non-empty Spanish word carrying no engine token, no English, no em dash, no data punctuation.
Token tuple is declared locally and asserted equal to the engine Factor union at the publish boundary, never imported from scoring.
steps.scenario_name: La frase está en español y no filtra nada del código
steps.non_visual_rationale: A pure token to word map with no markup and no layout; the words first become visible in 01-05, which carries the charter and the U1 to U7 checks.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, adapted): unit tests are property-based with fast-check, the house style at tests/unit/scoring-laws.test.ts; example-based tests are fallback only with a documented reason; integration and E2E stay single-example. Adapted from the Hypothesis wording because this repo is TypeScript with fast-check. DISPATCH: project CLAUDE.md declares the functional paradigm and selects @nw-functional-software-crafter for every DELIVER step; the agent field carries the schema-valid name and the orchestrator maps it. WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AND WHY HERE: R28 requires the Spanish factor names to come from ONE shared vocabulary module, seamed with F-KNOW-HOW-MUCH-TO-TRUST-IT, whose confidence_reason copy names the same four factors (05-scoring-engine.md section 3.6). The house home for such a module is src/data (the src/data/report-vocab.ts precedent), and src/data/** is a FORBIDDEN WRITE LANE for this build. So the module lands at src/publish/factor-vocab.ts and is SHAPED FOR THE MOVE: zero imports, tokens declared locally as a const tuple exactly like WIND_STATE_TOKENS. src/data/report-vocab.ts lines 29-30 state the rule that makes this load-bearing: a module under src/data may never import from src/publish/** or src/scoring/**, so a vocab module that imported Factor from src/scoring/engine could not be moved without an edit. The equality assertion between the local token tuple and the engine Factor union lives on the publish side, mirroring static-surface.ts line 19 (WindState = WindStateToken). CROSS-FEATURE DEPENDENCY, FLAGGED NOT FIXED: extracting this module to src/data/factor-vocab.ts and pointing both features at it is owed to whoever owns src/data/**; it is a git mv plus one import path change by construction. COPY SHAPE: export the bare noun (dirección, tamaño, viento, marea) AND the definite article per token, because this feature needs 'el viento' inside a sentence while the confidence lane needs the bare noun inside its own. Do not invent further copy here.

steps.name: SurfaceCall carries the published culprit token
criteria: SurfaceCall gains an optional weakest_link field typed as the vocabulary token or null, documented as the reading-surface half of the day summary.
assertStrictTwoDayUpdate accepts a surface whose rows carry the field and still accepts rows without it, so retained dawn receipts keep validating.
Property: adding or omitting the field never changes any other published field and never changes the two-day or distinct-ranking refusals.
Step does not populate the field; population is the serialized cross-lane build.ts edit recorded in this roadmap.
steps.scenario_name: El punto débil llega a la superficie que leen las páginas, no solo al recibo
steps.non_visual_rationale: A wire-type field and its validator behaviour; nothing renders. The value it carries becomes visible in 01-05, which owns the charter and the U1 to U7 checks.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, adapted): property-based with fast-check as in 01-01 over the validator laws; single-example fallback only with a documented reason. THIS STEP CANNOT TURN ITS SCENARIO GREEN ON THIS LANE'S FILES, AND MUST NOT PRETEND TO. Scenario 5 (@in-memory) drives runIngestOnce/runBuildOnce and asserts that bundle.publish_surface.days[i].spots[j].weakest_link equals bundle.days[i].spots[j].weakest_link. publish_surface is constructed inline at src/pipeline/build.ts lines 141-151 from surfaceCall(), a module-private function at lines 255-266; the bundle is written straight to the store at line 153 with no hook a publish-side module could reach. src/pipeline/build.ts is a FORBIDDEN WRITE LANE here. The scenario goes green only when this ONE line lands in surfaceCall()'s returned object, immediately after 'best_window: call.best_window,' on line 264:      weakest_link: call.weakest_link,      That is a SERIALIZED CROSS-LANE DEPENDENCY on the keystone/producer lane that owns build.ts (feature-delta Pre-requisite 1). Do not edit build.ts to unblock this step; report the block and continue with 01-03 onward, which are independent of it. WHY THE TYPE STILL SHIPS HERE: without the optional field on SurfaceCall the producer lane's one-liner does not typecheck, so this step is the half that makes the cross-lane line a one-liner instead of a two-file change. R3 SECOND HALF, DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED HERE: the requirement checklist marks R3 partially covered and names the gap, that a real pipeline run populates every committed row. tests/unit/published-surface-fields.test.ts is the existing guard family for exactly that class and it reads the COMMITTED data/published-surface.json on purpose (its header lines 8 to 11). Extending it to weakest_link TODAY would turn the unit suite red on trunk for every other lane, because the committed file carries zero occurrences right now. So that guard is owed IN THE SAME CHANGE as the build.ts one-liner, once a real build repopulates the file; it is recorded as a cross-lane follow-up, not planted red here.

steps.name: Reader resolves the culprit per spot and day
criteria: A pure publish-side reader answers, for one spot id and one day index, the published culprit token or null, never a derived or guessed one.
Today resolves from current.calls and tomorrow from current.days[1].spots, matching src/data/forecast.ts line 77 exactly, pinned by a unit test.
Property: a spot absent from the surface, a null field and an absent field all answer null; no input yields a fabricated factor.
Property: each spot answers only from its own published row; one row's culprit never leaks into another spot or the other day.
steps.scenario_name: Ninguna playa se queda callada mientras las demás sí lo dicen
steps.non_visual_rationale: A pure lookup over the committed reading surface with no markup; its output becomes visible in 01-05, which carries the charter and the U1 to U7 checks.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, adapted): property-based with fast-check over the resolution laws; single-example only for the committed-file smoke read. WHY A SECOND READER EXISTS, STATED PLAINLY SO NOBODY OVER-READS IT: the architecturally correct home for this carry is DaySummary in src/data/forecast.ts, which is the declared P1 render source SpotDetail.astro already consumes. src/data/** is a FORBIDDEN WRITE LANE for this build, so the carry lands in src/publish/**, which the lane declares as the surface plumbing. THE DRIFT HAZARD THIS CREATES, AND ITS ONLY MITIGATION: src/data/forecast.ts line 77 reads days as [summaries(current.calls), summaries(current.days[1].spots)] - today comes from the LEGACY calls alias and tomorrow from days[1].spots. That quirk is a compatibility alias for the yesterday and receipt readers, not an accident. This reader must replicate it, not the more obvious days[0]/days[1]. THE ACCEPTANCE SUITE CANNOT CATCH A MISTAKE HERE: applyPublishedCulprits in the step file plants the same today plan into BOTH current.calls and current.days[0].spots, so either reading passes all eleven scenarios. That makes the day-selection rule a UNIT-TEST OBLIGATION with a comment naming forecast.ts line 77 as the twin, and the failure it prevents is the page showing the wrong day's culprit, which is exactly the two-surfaces-must-not-disagree rule of application-architecture.md section 7 lines 320-323. CROSS-LANE FOLLOW-UP, FLAGGED: the day src/data/forecast.ts opens, DaySummary should absorb weakest_link and this module should collapse to nothing but the formatter, deleting the duplicated day-selection rule. Record it; do not perform it. IMPORT SHAPE: read the committed surface the same way forecast.ts does; the module graph already contains that JSON, so this adds no second parse of a different artifact. LEAK RULE: this module lives on the forecast side and the report flow must never reach it, directly or transitively (application-architecture.md sections 7 to 9).

steps.name: Spanish culprit sentence from one swappable constant
criteria: A house display formatter turns one factor token into the settled Spanish sentence; no component and no page ever composes that sentence inline.
The wording lives in exactly one exported constant so the pending copy settlement is a one-line swap, never an edit across files.
Property: for every factor token the sentence names that factor in Spanish and carries no engine token, no English word, no em dash, no double hyphen.
Property: the sentence never contains braces, brackets or quotation marks, and never the words null, undefined or NaN.
steps.scenario_name: La página nombra el culpable publicado, nunca uno que deduzca ella sola
steps.non_visual_rationale: Pure string composition behind the house never-format-inline discipline; the sentence reaches pixels in 01-05, which carries the charter and the U1 to U7 checks.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM (mandatory, adapted): property-based with fast-check across all four tokens; the settled-wording example is a single-example anchor with a documented reason. WHY HERE: SpotDetail.astro's own header lines 8 to 12 state the house rule that size and window are always rendered through src/publish/display-format.ts and never formatted by hand, so every surface says the same thing about the same wave. The culprit sentence joins that discipline; the Reuse Analysis row for display-format already anticipates it. OPEN COPY ITEM (feature-delta Pre-requisite 3), do not close it: 'Lo que lo tumba' appears nowhere in the repo and the settled section 14 wireframe carries '← el punto débil'. No scenario pins the wording; the acceptance assertions require ONLY that the Spanish factor noun appears inside the callout (steps file FACTOR_WORD, fixture factor_words). Write the recommended sentence from Pre-requisite 3 minus the number, which belongs to slice-02: 'Lo que lo tumba: el viento.' with the article and noun coming from 01-01's vocabulary. HOLD IT IN ONE EXPORTED CONSTANT so Andres's settlement through the cousin's crew channel is a one-line swap; do not invent flowery product copy and do not add the sub-score, which is slice-02's promise. STRINGS BOUNDARY CONFLICT, FLAGGED NOT FIXED: the project rule and the feature plan both say UI strings land in src/i18n/strings.ts so F-READ-IT-IN-YOUR-LANGUAGE translates one surface later, and src/i18n/** is a FORBIDDEN WRITE LANE for this build. The same conflict was handled this way on the sibling lane (define once in the allowed lane, flag the consolidation). Record the move of this constant into strings.ts as a cross-lane follow-up owed to the i18n owner. ASSERTION TRAPS worth pinning as properties: the steps file rejects a double hyphen as well as an em dash (EM_DASH = /[—]|--/), rejects data punctuation /[{}\[\]"]/, and its CODE_LEAK word list includes the bare English words the, today and tomorrow as well as the four engine tokens.

steps.name: Callout component renders per day section
criteria: A new self-contained component renders one visible element carrying data-field weakest-link, holding the Spanish sentence for that spot and that day.
Each day section shows its own day's culprit; today's is never tomorrow's and tomorrow's is never today's on the same page.
The element is genuinely rendered, not merely emitted: text is readable through innerText, never only present in the markup.
All markup, logic and scoped styling live in the component; the spot page receives only the import and the mount.
steps.scenario_name: El surfista abre su playa y lee qué la tumbó hoy y qué la tumba mañana
steps.u8_observation: Abro mi playa en el teléfono y en la sección de hoy leo, en una frase tranquila y terminada, qué fue lo que la tumbó; en la sección de mañana leo la de mañana, y ninguna de las dos me repite la del otro día. No parece una anotación de programador: parece parte de la página.
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: publish-time markup composition, single-shot by nature and not unit-testable without a component-container harness this lane will not introduce; compensated by the property-based tests on the vocabulary (01-01), the reader (01-03) and the formatter (01-04), and by ten browser scenarios over the emitted dist. MARKUP CONTRACT, fixed by DISTILL and non-negotiable: exactly ONE element per day section, located by section[data-day="today"] [data-field="weakest-link"] and its tomorrow twin, following the house data-field convention already used by score, size and window. Props are the spot id and the day index; the component asks 01-03 for the token and 01-04 for the sentence and does no lookup, no arithmetic and no derivation of its own. INNERTEXT IS LOAD-BEARING: every oracle reads innerText, never textContent, precisely so that markup which ships but never renders visibly reads as an empty box rather than as a pass. Do not render it hidden, zero-sized, clipped or behind display:none. This repo's worst shipped bug passed all ten CI jobs; that shape is closed here on purpose. ZERO NEW JAVASCRIPT: the element renders at publish time (adr-publish-time-html-rendering.md); the spot route's JS budget must not move. STYLING: scoped styles inside the component using named tokens only (09-design-system.md line 237). Do NOT edit src/styles/** - it is outside this lane's declared boundary; the bar recipe at src/styles/recipes.css belongs to slice-04 and is not needed for a sentence. THE MOUNT IS ANOTHER LANE'S FILE AND IS THREE LINES, NOT ONE. src/components/SpotDetail.astro is owned by the concurrent BUGFIX lane (worktree /Users/andres/psb-bugfix, branch build/f2-bugfix) and by keystone slice-06; it is a FORBIDDEN WRITE LANE here. Hand this exact delta to whoever lands it, as a serialized cross-lane edit: (a) frontmatter, new line after line 18 (the display-format import): import WeakestLink from './WeakestLink.astro'; (b) inside section[data-day="today"], new line after line 72 (the today window paragraph), indented ten spaces: <WeakestLink spotId={spotId} day={0} /> (c) inside section[data-day="tomorrow"], new line after line 86 (the tomorrow window paragraph), indented ten spaces: <WeakestLink spotId={spotId} day={1} /> Both mounts sit INSIDE the existing day-summary fragment, so a spot with no summary for that day keeps its current sentence and gains no callout. R4 DISCREPANCY, FLAGGED LOUDLY: R4 and the feature-delta say 'exactly one mount line', and the markup contract requires an element inside EACH day section while Astro requires an import, so the honest delta is three added lines. Nothing in the component moves that number to one. The RED classification already demoted R4's one-line half to a DELIVER code-review constraint because it is not observable through the built surface; this is the code-review fact it needs.

steps.name: Perfect day renders no callout element
criteria: When the published culprit is explicitly null, neither day section renders any weakest-link element: none empty, none hidden, none at all.
The page shows no stray word and no code word where the culprit would go; score, size and window still render for both days.
A sibling beach published in the same morning still names its own culprit, so silence is that row's, never the whole render's.
The absence reads as a designed state at 390 px: no empty box, no dangling label, no artificial loading.
steps.scenario_name: Un día perfecto no tiene culpable, y la página no parece rota por eso
steps.u8_observation: Abro una playa que salió perfecta y sencillamente no hay frase de culpable, ni un recuadro vacío ni una palabra suelta donde iría; la página se ve completa, con su puntaje, su tamaño y su ventana, y la playa de al lado sigue diciendo el suyo.
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: one designed UI state; compensated by 01-03's property that a null field resolves to null. THE ORACLE COUNTS ELEMENTS, NOT TEXT: the step file asserts todayCount and tomorrowCount are both 0 for this beach, so rendering an empty element, or an element hidden by CSS, FAILS. The component must emit nothing at all for a null culprit. This is the settled degrade, not an invention: application-architecture.md section 7 line 294 and src/publish/region-bundle.ts line 52, 'never a fabricated culprit'. weakest_link is null exactly when every factor damage is 0 (05-scoring-engine.md section 4, law L10), which is a perfect day, not missing data. WHY THIS SCENARIO CANNOT PASS VACUOUSLY, and why that matters to the crafter: an absence assertion is trivially true against a page that renders nothing at all, so the scenario closes on a sibling beach from the same published morning that MUST name its culprit. A component that silently renders nothing everywhere fails on the sibling, not here. The fixture beach is playa-guanico with an explicit null on both days; the sibling is playa-venao. The same walk also asserts the rest of the day section survives, so the callout must be a sibling element in the section, never a wrapper around score, size or window. Also pinned: no null, undefined or NaN anywhere in the page body text.

steps.name: Absent field stays silent, page reads complete
criteria: When the published row carries no culprit field at all, neither day section renders a weakest-link element and no raw error reaches the page.
The page is not blank and shows no TypeError, ReferenceError or server-error text; today's score still renders.
A missing field is treated as a normal page state, never as a render failure and never as a reason to invent a culprit.
A sibling beach published in the same morning still names its own culprit.
steps.scenario_name: Una playa cuya mañana se publicó sin ese dato calla en vez de inventar
steps.u8_observation: Abro una playa cuya mañana se publicó sin ese dato y la página simplemente no dice nada del culpable: se lee entera, con su puntaje, sin un error crudo ni un hueco en blanco, y la playa de al lado sí nombra el suyo.
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: a second designed UI state over a different input shape; compensated by 01-03's property that an absent field resolves to null. WHY THIS IS NOT A DUPLICATE OF 01-06: 01-06's beach publishes weakest_link: null explicitly; this beach (playa-reina) has the KEY DELETED from its rows entirely, which is what happens on a surface written before the field existed - the state the committed data/published-surface.json is in today, with zero occurrences of weakest_link. The optional field on SurfaceCall means TypeScript will not warn; the reader must answer null for a missing key exactly as for an explicit null, and the component must render nothing either way. The distinct oracle here is that the page reads COMPLETE: not blank, no raw error text, today's score non-empty. That closes the honest degrade of application-architecture.md section 7 line 295, and it is the same failure class as the 19-of-20 missing-optional-fields bug this repo already shipped green: the surface must degrade to silence, never to 'undefined'. Do not add a placeholder sentence, a dash, a skeleton or an aria-only label for the absent case; the settled degrade is nothing at all.

steps.name: Callout mounts on spot page only
criteria: Today's ranked list renders zero weakest-link elements and its content is otherwise unchanged.
The same beach's own page names its culprit in the same visit, so the list's silence is scope, not a missing feature.
The component is referenced by the spot page only; no other route, layout or component imports it.
The ranked list source is not edited at all in this slice.
steps.scenario_name: El culpable aparece en la página de la playa y no cambia la lista de hoy
steps.u8_observation: Miro la lista de hoy y se ve exactamente como siempre, sin ninguna frase de culpable; entro a la playa y ahí sí me dice qué la tumbó. El aviso vive en la página de la playa y en ningún otro lado.
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: a scoping guard over built artifacts; the acceptance oracle counts elements on the emitted home document. THE OBSERVABLE HALF OF R4. The oracle counts [data-field="weakest-link"] across the WHOLE home document and requires 0, then opens the spot page and requires the culprit. So the containment rule is: the component is mounted by the spot page and by nothing else. src/components/RankedList.astro is DO NOT TOUCH in the Reuse Analysis and is a FORBIDDEN WRITE LANE here; it is also owned right now by the concurrent BUGFIX lane. The settled section 14 home wireframe carries no weakest-link element, and adding one is a new DISCUSS decision, not scope creep. THE FALSIFIABILITY PASS BELONGS HERE (project rule: prove every negative falsifiable). This scenario's list half passes today against a page that renders nothing anywhere, so after 01-05 lands, deliberately mount the component into the list, watch this scenario fail for the right reason, revert, and verify the revert with git diff. Record the observation. Do not leave the experiment behind. NOTE FOR THE CODE REVIEW: the mount itself is the cross-lane SpotDetail.astro delta recorded in 01-05; this step verifies its containment, it does not perform it.

steps.name: Words carry the callout, never colour
criteria: With every colour signal flattened to one ink on one paper, both day sections still name their factor in readable Spanish words.
The factor name lives in the element's own text, never in a swatch, an icon, a border tint or a background alone.
No colour, weight or position is the sole carrier of which factor is named.
The flattened reading is taken through innerText, so markup present but not rendered reads as empty and fails.
steps.scenario_name: Quien no distingue colores recibe la misma información
steps.u8_observation: Con la pantalla lavada, sin un solo color, sigo leyendo en palabras qué tumbó la playa hoy y qué la tumba mañana: la información no dependía del color, estaba escrita.
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: an accessibility invariant asserted over the rendered surface; compensated by 01-04's property that every factor token composes to a sentence naming it in Spanish words. THE DESIGN LAW: 09-design-system.md line 237 - the weakest link is named by the arrow plus words, and colour never carries the callout alone. Slice-01 ships the WORDS half; the arrow and the bars are slice-04 and must not be pre-built here. WHAT THE HARNESS ACTUALLY DOES: it injects a stylesheet forcing every colour, background, border, fill, stroke and shadow to one ink on one paper, then re-reads the callout through innerText. After that only text survives, so a culprit conveyed by a coloured swatch, an icon, a border tint, or by markup that is present but never rendered, reads as empty and fails. Do not read this as a colour-blindness simulation; it is the honest way to assert the factor is named in words. PRACTICAL CONSEQUENCE for the component: the factor noun must sit in the element's own text node. An aria-label, a title attribute, a CSS ::before content string or a background image is NOT the words - innerText does not return them. This step touches display-format.ts only if 01-04's sentence needs the factor noun moved inside the visible text rather than an adjacent decorated element; if 01-04 already satisfies it, this step is the explicit verification pass and the formatter is left unchanged.

steps.name: Seven visual checks, both themes, real backdrop
criteria: Both callout sentences clear 4.5:1 against the nearest non-transparent ancestor background, in light theme and in dark theme.
Type comes from the declared scale: at least 14 px with line height at least 1.2 times the size, surviving the longest Spanish spot name.
No horizontal overflow at 390 px; the report call to action still measures at least 44 by 44 px and is not displaced.
Under reduced motion the callout carries no transition and no animation; no artificial loading inside it; no raw colour in its style attribute.
The repository UI quality gate exits 0 for the built surface.
steps.scenario_name: La frase se lee en el teléfono, en los dos temas, con el nombre de playa más largo
steps.u8_observation: En Santa Catalina - La Punta, a 390 px, la frase del culpable se lee cómoda en tema claro y en tema oscuro, sin que nada se salga de la pantalla ni se corte; con movimiento reducido nada se anima, y el botón de reportar sigue donde estaba y del mismo tamaño.
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM: measured UI quality over built artifacts; the browser oracle and the repository gate are the instruments. ONE SCENARIO OUTLINE, TWO EXAMPLE ROWS, BOTH OWNED BY THIS STEP: | claro | normal | and | oscuro | reducido |. Both must pass; the dark row also carries prefers-reduced-motion. CONTRAST IS MEASURED AGAINST THE REAL BACKDROP, not white: the audit walks up from the callout to the nearest ancestor whose computed background is not transparent, so a token that only clears AA on paper will fail on a card. Both themes, so pick tokens that hold in both. THE COUNT GUARD FIRES FIRST: the audit compares the number of callout elements found against the number the published plan expects (two for this beach, which publishes size today and wind tomorrow), and reports 'nothing to measure' before any contrast maths runs - so a missing render can never read as 'AA is fine'. U3 has TWO halves: any interactive element the callout adds must measure 44 px, and the existing thumb-zone report call to action (a.cta) must still measure 44 by 44 and not be displaced or occluded. THE SIMPLEST WAY TO HOLD BOTH: ship no interactive element inside the callout at all - slice-01 promises a sentence, not a control, and the 'por qué' reason tap is explicitly F-KNOW-HOW-MUCH-TO-TRUST-IT's. U7 forbids raw colour in the element's own style attribute, and the repository gate scripts/check-ui-quality.mjs owns the no-raw-hex-outside-src/styles rule and must exit 0 for the built surface; scripts/** is a FORBIDDEN WRITE LANE, so the gate is run, never edited. U2 uses the longest Spanish spot name, Santa Catalina - La Punta: let the sentence wrap rather than forcing it onto one line. GATE DISCIPLINE, this repo has committed over a red gate through a pipeline before: run npm run test:at -- --tags "@feature-f-see-what-killed-it and @slice-01" with output redirected to a file, capture $? on its own line, then read the file; never pipe a gate into tail, head or grep. Expect 11 scenarios, 0 failed, real exit 0 - except that scenario 5 stays red until the serialized cross-lane build.ts line lands (see 01-02), which is a BLOCK to report, not a reason to edit a forbidden file. Then run npm run test:at -- --tags "not @feature-f-see-what-killed-it" and confirm the other 78 scenarios still pass. AFTER GREEN: npm run build and INSPECT what actually renders in dist (project rule: green tests do not mean it works; the conf_level bug shipped green on all ten jobs). COMMIT IS BLOCKED until the slice charter exists - see the charter gap recorded in this roadmap - because the source-blind examiner is dispatched with the charter and its U8 observation and nothing else.

phases.name: Slice-02: the named factor carries its published raw value
phases.description: One scalar follows the already-published weakest-link label from the producer to the existing callout. The page formats it but never chooses, derives, rescales or fetches it. Full sub-score disclosure remains Slice-04.

steps.name: Optional published culprit-score field is typed and guarded
criteria: SurfaceCall adds optional weakest_link_subscore only for a named weakest_link: finite 0 through 1, while legacy named rows without it remain valid.
A present scalar never changes any existing reading-surface field, two-day validation, rank order or retained-dawn behavior.
Property: valid named scalars survive unchanged; null or missing weakest links, NaN, infinity and out-of-range values are rejected when paired with the scalar.
The field is documented as the raw score for the already-published weakest_link, not a second factor choice and not the Slice-04 four-factor record.
steps.scenario_name: La playa lee el valor publicado de la misma cosa que la tumbó
steps.non_visual_rationale: This is the backward-compatible reading-surface wire type. Pixels first change in 02-04, which owns the charter and all U1 to U7 checks.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: use fast-check property tests at the pure strict-validator boundary with a state-delta universe covering the supplied call, day ordering and validation result. Do not import scoring internals into the static-surface type. The schema owner must accept X7 before this step turns green; this step is the consumer-side type and validation half only.

steps.name: Producer carries the raw value beside its named factor
criteria: Every freshly built named weakest-link row carries weakest_link_subscore selected from CallRow.sub with the same factor key; no page computes or selects this value.
A null weakest_link carries no scalar, while a named weakest_link with null, non-finite or out-of-range matching sub-score refuses publication before the reading surface changes.
Property: changing any unselected factor score does not change the carried scalar; changing the named factor score changes only that scalar.
The committed newly built surface proves every named spot-day has the scalar and every clean spot-day omits it.
steps.scenario_name: El número sale de la misma mañana que nombró el culpable
steps.non_visual_rationale: A producer projection and publication invariant; the number becomes visible only through 02-04.
steps.implementation_notes: SERIALIZED CROSS-LANE STEP: build.ts and the committed surface belong to the producer/schema owner. Select call.sub[call.weakest_link] only while both values are in the pipeline record; that selection is a published-data projection, not frontend derivation. Do not carry the complete sub object, add an hourly lookup, or change the ranked row selection.

steps.name: Reader preserves the one row and one day pairing
criteria: The publish-side reader returns a named factor with its own raw scalar only when both arrive on the same selected spot-day row.
Today continues to read current.calls and tomorrow current.days[1].spots, matching forecast.ts exactly.
Property: another factor's lower score never replaces the named scalar; an absent scalar omits the numeric suffix, never guesses a value.
Clean and unknown weakest-link states retain their existing semantics and cannot acquire a number.
steps.scenario_name: El número acompaña al factor publicado, no al más bajo
steps.non_visual_rationale: A pure reader law. The visible number is owned by 02-04.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: fast-check over independently varied day rows and factors. Preserve the tagged clean and unknown states instead of introducing a nullable primitive. The implementation must read one row once, not call a separate factor selector or inspect spot_detail hourly data.

steps.name: One formatter extends the existing callout sentence
criteria: The house formatter appends the selected raw score as ', a 0.18' to the named Spanish sentence, using exactly two decimal places and no inline page formatting.
The existing one callout element changes text only; it gains no new mount, control, JavaScript, client fetch, route change or extra element.
A legacy named row without the scalar keeps a complete Spanish factor sentence with no dangling punctuation, code token, English, null or undefined.
Property: values 0 through 1 render as two-place decimals and the formatter never substitutes another factor's value.
steps.scenario_name: El surfista ve el valor de la misma cosa que la tumbó
steps.u8_observation: El número vive dentro de una sola frase clara en español. Se lee como una razón para surfear o no, no como telemetría ni una nota de programador.
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM for the markup edit: the existing component is publish-time static composition; compensate with properties in the formatter and reader plus future built-surface acceptance checks. Create the stated expectation charter only when Slice-02 enters JIT DISTILL, then run U1-U7 and a fresh U8 examiner before COMMIT. Do not change SpotDetail.astro: Slice-01 already owns the sole mount.

steps.name: Built surface proves the raw value and its honest degrades
criteria: The future acceptance run proves today and tomorrow render distinct named-factor values from their own published rows at 390 px.
A fixture where tide is numerically lower but wind is the published weakest link proves the page shows wind's raw value, not a frontend minimum.
Legacy named rows omit only the numeric suffix; perfect and unknown days remain element-free as Slice-01 already promises.
The two-theme, reduced-motion, overflow, type, target and token checks pass with the longer number-bearing sentence, and the route adds zero JavaScript.
steps.scenario_name: La playa muestra el valor publicado sin inventar uno
steps.u8_observation: En un teléfono leo qué tumbó la playa y su valor en la misma frase. Cuando ese valor no llegó en una mañana vieja, la frase sigue completa sin un hueco extraño ni una cifra inventada.
steps.implementation_notes: JIT DISTILL ONLY: do not author these test files while mapping. On legal entry, add five example-based real-I/O scenarios from slice-02-contract.md, run the explicit RED classification, and leave every Slice-01 test and evidence unchanged. The two browser negative cases make the missing field and false-minimum failures falsifiable.

phases.name: Slice-03: the callout states the honest score without its named weakness
phases.description: The producer computes one correction-aware counterfactual score from the already-owned damage record, carries it as an optional integer, and the existing callout renders it only when it is strictly higher. No browser arithmetic and no full breakdown enter this slice.

steps.name: Counterfactual integer is an authorized optional surface field
criteria: After X8 approval, SurfaceCall accepts optional counterfactual_score_q only with a named weakest_link and only as an integer from 0 through 100 greater than score_q.
An absent field remains valid for retained dawn receipts and older named rows; a clean day or an equal, lower, fractional or out-of-range field is rejected when present.
Property: valid named rows retain every existing observable field and counterfactual_score_q unchanged through strict two-day validation.
The field is documented as a producer-decided score without the named weakness, never as frontend arithmetic or the Slice-04 damage disclosure.
steps.scenario_name: La playa solo recibe un puntaje sin su punto débil cuando es más alto
steps.non_visual_rationale: This is the backward-compatible reading-surface contract. Pixels first change in 03-05, which owns the expectation charter and U1 through U7 checks.
steps.implementation_notes: SERIALIZED SCHEMA STEP: wait for X8's schema-authority approval. Use fast-check at the strict-validator boundary with a state-delta universe covering call fields, days and validation outcome. Do not use a truthy check: zero is within the field's raw range even though this particular field requires a strictly higher integer than score_q.

steps.name: Pure correction-aware counterfactual preserves scoring laws
criteria: A pure helper derives the integer from total log damage, the named factor damage and the build correction delta using the settled formula.
Property: whenever a named factor exists, the unrounded counterfactual is never below the displayed model score before publication suppression.
Property: with delta_q zero, the helper is bit-exact to round(100 times exp(-(D minus d_w))); the settled size example yields 93.
A missing named factor yields no candidate, and malformed damage input fails at the producer boundary rather than fabricating a number.
steps.scenario_name: El número sin el punto débil sigue la misma cuenta que publicó la mañana
steps.non_visual_rationale: Pure scoring behavior with no markup. The visible sentence is deferred to 03-05.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: fast-check over the existing L10 generator domain with state-delta assertions over returned candidate, damage inputs and correction value. The pipeline remains the only caller that publishes it; extracting a pure helper keeps arithmetic testable without moving publication decisions into the page.

steps.name: Producer carries only a meaningful counterfactual score
criteria: The build computes the candidate while ScoreResult damages and the applied correction are in scope, then carries counterfactual_score_q only when it is strictly greater than score_q.
Fresh named rows carry the integer or deliberately omit it for a rounding collision; fresh clean rows omit it. A candidate below score_q refuses publication before artifacts advance.
Property: changing the named factor's damage or correction changes only the counterfactual projection, while unrelated published fields retain their values.
A newly built committed surface proves every present field is integral, greater than its row score and paired with a named weakest link.
steps.scenario_name: La mañana publica solo un puntaje sin culpable que de verdad mejora
steps.non_visual_rationale: Producer projection and data-integrity behavior. The value becomes visible only in 03-05.
steps.implementation_notes: SERIALIZED CROSS-LANE STEP: the producer and committed surface belong to the schema/producer owner. Compute before CallRow drops damages. Do not recover the value from the page, from hourly data, or by re-running scoring after publication. This step also closes X5's populated-per-build requirement for weakest_link where that producer change is available.

steps.name: Reader keeps the counterfactual paired to its spot-day
criteria: The publish-side reader exposes a counterfactual only from the same selected row as the named weakest link and its score_q.
Today reads current.calls and tomorrow reads current.days[1].spots, preserving the forecast.ts compatibility rule.
Property: another day's number, a clean day and a collision omission never create a reading; named legacy absence stays distinct.
The reader performs no exponential arithmetic, damage selection, score correction or full-subscore lookup.
steps.scenario_name: El número sin el punto débil pertenece a ese día y a esa playa
steps.non_visual_rationale: A pure read contract. Text becomes visible in 03-05.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: fast-check independently varies both day rows and verifies the tagged reader state. Preserve clean and unknown outcomes, and make named legacy absence distinct so the publish-time caller logs it once. No new selector, factor resolver or browser lookup belongs here.

steps.name: Existing callout renders the day-aware honest clause
criteria: The display formatter appends one day-aware Spanish counterfactual clause using the published integer verbatim; it does not calculate a score.
The existing weakest-link element changes text only, with no new mount, control, route, client fetch, island or JavaScript.
Absent, clean and collision states retain a complete named sentence or no callout as appropriate, with no empty gap, dangling punctuation, raw token, English, null or undefined.

A named legacy row without counterfactual_score_q omits only the clause and records one health.publish.counterfactual_field_missing event with spot, day and publish stamp; it adds no client telemetry.
At 390 px in both themes, the longer sentence remains readable against its real backdrop and leaves the report call to action reachable.
steps.scenario_name: El surfista lee cuánto marcaría la playa sin ese punto débil
steps.u8_observation: La segunda frase se siente como una explicación tranquila de la misma llamada. Hoy y mañana usan sus propias palabras y números, sin parecer una promesa técnica ni una nota de programador.
steps.implementation_notes: EXEMPT FROM PARADIGM for the static markup edit. Compensate with properties in 03-02 and 03-04 plus future built-surface checks. The build-side compatibility event follows the health.publish structured-log convention, has no metric or browser transport, and is asserted from build output. Do not settle copy or edit SpotDetail.astro.

steps.name: Built surface proves the counterfactual and every suppression
criteria: The future acceptance run proves both day sections show their own published higher counterfactual integers through the built production surface at 390 px.
A correction-aware fixture proves the producer carries the formula with delta_q, and a lower-than-score mutation refuses publication instead of rendering a lie.
Rounding collision and perfect day suppress only the clause; named legacy absence also emits one health.publish.counterfactual_field_missing event without client telemetry.
The two-theme, reduced-motion, overflow, type, target and token checks pass with the longer sentence and the route adds zero JavaScript.
steps.scenario_name: La playa explica la mejora sin inventar una cifra
steps.u8_observation: En un teléfono puedo leer la mejora de hoy y la de mañana como parte natural de cada llamada. Cuando no hay una mejora honesta que mostrar, no queda una frase vacía ni una cifra repetida.
steps.implementation_notes: JIT DISTILL ONLY: do not author these test files while mapping. On legal entry, add the six example-based real-I/O behaviors in slice-03-contract.md, record the RED classification and preserve all Slice-01 and Slice-02 evidence. The lower-score mutation must fail the producer before the page oracle, proving no impossible value can ship.

phases.name: Slice-04: the spot page explains the best window with four honest bars
phases.description: The published hourly record becomes the only source for four best-window bars. The static page selects one already-scored hour, states missing observations as absences, and keeps the existing weakest-link decision authoritative. No browser scoring, averaging, fetch, island, or route change enters this phase.

steps.name: Hourly best-window projection is an authorized reading-surface seam
criteria: After X9 approval, BundleSpotDetail and SurfaceSpotDetail accept an optional hourly array of exactly the publish-time two-day horizon, with one spot-local offset timestamp t and a four-key sub record per point.
Each sub record has finite 0..1 values or null; null remains an absence, never zero or a best-case value.
The shape carries only t and sub to the reading surface. It adds no raw observations, damages, score-selection rule, browser time-zone rule, or second ranking.
Legacy spot_detail entries without hourly remain valid and distinguishable so retained surfaces can degrade by omission instead of failing a whole spot page.
steps.scenario_name: El desglose llega completo desde la mañana que publicó la llamada
steps.non_visual_rationale: This is the backward-compatible wire contract. Visible bars first arrive in 04-05, which owns the charter and U1 through U7 checks.
steps.implementation_notes: SERIALIZED SCHEMA STEP: X9 is required because domain-model.md section 13 declares hourly[] as the intended P1 source while its implemented-name table says spot_detail currently ships name only. Define the additive point as { t: string, sub: { dir: number, size: number, wind: number | null, tide: number | null } }; t is the precomputed spot-local ISO timestamp with numeric offset shown by the authoritative payload example, not a browser-local conversion. Use fast-check at the strict-validator boundary. Do not add acceptance files or make the legacy optional shape mandatory.

steps.name: Producer projects each scored hour without substituting missing factors
criteria: The build creates the 48-point per-spot hourly projection from the same CallRow sub values that the scoring core produced, preserving the point timestamp and every null exactly.
Every freshly built surface has one projection point for each scored hour spanning its two published civil days, and each point uses the spot's precomputed local offset timestamp.
Property: changing one CallRow sub value changes only that matching projection point's matching sub field; it changes neither day ranking, weakest_link, best_window nor any other point.
A null wind or tide remains null in the projected sub record even when the separately rendered wind-state word is absent; the repaired windState mapping from ee61840 remains green.
steps.scenario_name: Un dato ausente sigue ausente en el desglose
steps.non_visual_rationale: This producer projection is invisible until the static reader and bars mount in 04-05.
steps.implementation_notes: Use the 48 scored CallRows already held by the build, not a new upstream query or a second scoring pass. The currently open Pre-requisite 2 wording is stale: commit ee61840 changed windState(null) to null and tests/unit/wind-state-honesty.test.ts verifies it. Treat that committed behavior as a required regression dependency, not work to redo. This is the serialized producer change that makes X9 real; do not republish a committed fixture in this mapping phase.

steps.name: Publish reader selects one declared best-window hour
criteria: A pure publish-side reader joins one selected spot-day summary to that spot's hourly projection and returns the four sub values from exactly the point whose precomputed local hour contains best_window.start.
It performs one point lookup only: no averaging, interpolation, re-scoring, damage selection, minimum-bar choice, browser time-zone conversion, or fallback to another hour is permitted.
A missing best_window, missing hourly field, absent matching hour, duplicated matching hour or malformed sub record returns an unavailable breakdown, never an invented factor value.
Property: a result from another spot, day or hour cannot enter the selected breakdown; the reader preserves null wind and tide as explicit missing-factor states.
steps.scenario_name: Cada día lee solo la hora que explica su ventana
steps.non_visual_rationale: A pure reading contract. The visible explanation is intentionally deferred to 04-05.
steps.implementation_notes: TEST PARADIGM: fast-check over independent spot, day and hourly inputs, with single examples for the offset-time join. Follow forecast.ts's today/current.calls and tomorrow/current.days[1].spots compatibility rule, but use the same selected day summary only as the source of best_window and weakest_link. Extracting the local hour from the already-published offset timestamp is a pure wire comparison, not client time computation. The reader must return a tagged unavailable reason for legacy hourly absence versus malformed current rows so the caller can log only the former compatibility gap.

steps.name: Four-factor breakdown formatter preserves authoritative weakness and absence
criteria: One formatter exposes four Spanish factor rows in the fixed dir, size, wind, tide order, using the selected published values verbatim to two decimal places and no scoring arithmetic.
A null factor becomes its explicit Spanish absence, for example sin dato de viento hoy, with no numeric label, zero-width or zero-height fill, fabricated wind word, null or undefined.
Only the day summary's published weakest_link marks the arrow row. No bar height, numerical minimum or null factor can select or replace that row.
The formatter returns present or unavailable. Legacy hourly absence logs one build-side health.publish.breakdown_hourly_missing event with spot, day and publish stamp, never browser telemetry.
steps.scenario_name: La flecha sigue el punto débil publicado, no la barra más baja
steps.non_visual_rationale: Formatting and structured compatibility logging make no pixels until the static component is mounted in 04-05.
steps.implementation_notes: Reuse Slice-01 factor-vocab and display-format seams. A visual fill percentage is presentation-only and must never affect which row gets the arrow. Preserve a strict distinction: best_window absent is the accepted normal omission; legacy hourly absent is a backward-compatibility gap that logs once during publish-time render; a malformed fresh hourly projection is a producer-contract error and must not be disguised as legacy. No copy beyond factor names and stated absences is authorized.

steps.name: Static spot page renders four honest best-window bars
criteria: A valid day renders one visible breakdown element with four named rows, published values or stated absences, and the published weakest-link arrow.
The page reuses the approved 8 px track, sunken background and weakest danger fill recipe; the arrow and factor words identify the weak row independently of colour.
No best_window yields no breakdown element or empty shell. A null wind or tide row visibly states its absence and has no fill, while the other three rows remain readable.
Both day sections use their own selected hour and weakest_link. No JavaScript, client fetch or island is added; the report action stays reachable at 390 px.
steps.scenario_name: El surfista lee cuatro razones de su mejor ventana sin una mentira por datos faltantes
steps.u8_observation: En mi teléfono veo hoy y mañana como dos explicaciones separadas. Las cuatro filas me dejan entender la mejor ventana y la flecha me dice cuál fue el problema real. Si falta el viento, la página lo dice en vez de fingir una barra buena o mala.
steps.implementation_notes: The create-new Breakdown component owns markup and scoped behavior. The SpotDetail import plus one mount in each existing day fragment is a serialized shared-host edit, recorded as X10. Move the existing unshipped .bars/.bar recipe from src/styles/recipes.css into the shipped component stylesheet in the same change, and do not edit recipes.css. The exact component locator is section[data-day="today"] [data-field="breakdown"] and its tomorrow twin. No client JS is allowed.

steps.name: Built surface proves the full disclosure and every honest omission
criteria: At 390 px, valid days have four rows, each printed number equals its published best-window-hour sub value, and each arrow follows weakest_link.
Missing-wind and missing-tide examples show Spanish absence with no fill or fabricated wind state; no best_window means no breakdown while its day summary survives.
Legacy hourly absence records exactly one health.publish.breakdown_hourly_missing event with no client telemetry; malformed fresh projections fail before a misleading built page ships.
The two themes, reduced motion, overflow, type, colour-independent weak-row indication, target reachability, token and zero-JavaScript checks pass for the full component.
steps.scenario_name: La playa expone sus cuatro razones sin recalcular ni inventar nada
steps.u8_observation: En un teléfono, las barras de hoy y mañana se sienten parte natural de la misma llamada. Puedo ver la razón débil sin depender del color y cuando falta un dato la frase es clara, no una cifra inventada.
steps.implementation_notes: JIT DISTILL ONLY: do not author future feature files, steps, fixtures, expectation charter, tags or RED-classification evidence while mapping. When Slice-04 legally opens, create six example-based production-build and browser behaviors from slice-04-contract.md, record RED against real ports, then implement one behavior at a time. Pure selector and formatter properties remain unit-level fast-check; browser and build failure cases remain pinned examples.

phases.name: Slice-05: the spot page carries a small, honest static break map
phases.description: One lazily loaded, pre-rendered static asset per launch spot shows the break and its seed-owned orientation. An approved imagery source and visible attribution are hard prerequisites. No visitor-time tile request, map library, geolocation, endpoint, or interactive map is introduced.

steps.name: Map source decision becomes a reproducible asset policy
criteria: After X11 approval, one tracked policy identifies an approved imagery source or accepted orientation-only fallback, with license, acquisition, visible attribution and refresh rules.
The policy enumerates each launch spot, coordinate provenance, asset identity and shore-normal provenance; a missing or contested input refuses that asset rather than guessing.
The policy fixes a stable generated asset path and attribution payload that the static page can consume without a runtime request or hidden third-party credit.
The decision records why the chosen path costs zero at serving time and why any rejected tile, browser-library, scraped or uncredited source cannot enter the build.
steps.scenario_name: Cada playa recibe un mapa con una fuente que sí podemos mostrar
steps.non_visual_rationale: The policy authorizes a later asset and does not change a rendered route. Visible map behavior starts in 05-04.
steps.implementation_notes: HARD DECISION GATE: do not select a provider by inference. X11 must choose the image-source path and exact attribution, or explicitly approve the seed-only orientation diagram as a changed product fulfillment. Existing seed coordinates are citable but source imagery is not. The policy must be committed with its license evidence reference; it is not a private build secret or a README footnote.

steps.name: Build creates bounded static map assets only
criteria: The approved policy drives a reproducible generator that emits one content-addressed WebP per eligible launch spot under public/maps, each at or under the settled 12 KB target.
Generation happens before the Astro route build and writes no network URL, tile template, provider token or map-library code into emitted spot HTML or browser JavaScript.
Property: an unchanged policy and seed reproduce the same asset manifest; changing one approved spot record changes only that spot asset identity and manifest row.
A failed fetch, missing attribution, invalid bytes, absent coordinate or unsupported content type fails the asset build before site publication, never by replacing the map with an unrelated image.
steps.scenario_name: El mapa que abre el surfista ya viene listo, sin pedir un mosaico
steps.non_visual_rationale: This is an asset-generation and build-boundary change. The page first exposes it in 05-04.
steps.implementation_notes: Use a content-addressed local output and a checked manifest, so an image revision cannot be served under a stale fixed path. The asset generator is a build-time adapter, never an Astro component concern. Do not introduce a dependency merely to rasterize a diagram before X11 says which legal path is in force. The ordinary page-weight gate must continue to exclude loading=lazy images from first-visit bytes while the map-specific asset test enforces the individual target.

steps.name: Map orientation is encoded from the declared spot seed
criteria: The generated map marks the same spot coordinates and the direction indicated by that spot's declared shore_normal_deg; it never infers orientation from a coastline picture or a generic regional arrow.
The marker and orientation arrow are baked into the approved static asset or the expressly accepted orientation-only diagram, so the page needs no map computation or script.
Property: rotating one seed orientation changes only its own generated arrow, not another spot, its map source, ranking, forecast or image dimensions contract.
A null, contested or out-of-range orientation refuses generation for that spot and leaves no deceptive map; the launch policy exclusion remains authoritative.
steps.scenario_name: La flecha del mapa sigue la orientación que conoce esa playa
steps.non_visual_rationale: The orientation transform is build-time asset behavior; its visible arrow and image arrive together in 05-04.
steps.implementation_notes: The current coordinate adapter reads lat/lon only; extend the map-specific build input deliberately rather than leaking map fields into src/data/region.ts, which remains report-safe identity. Coordinate, shore-normal and launch-policy validation happen at the asset boundary. Existing source seed comments say shore normals are derived and potentially uncertain, so the map may show only the declared orientation, never claim a more precise physical coastline fact.

steps.name: Static map component renders lazy image and visible credit
criteria: A self-contained spot-page component renders one meaningful Spanish figure with a local content-addressed WebP, loading=lazy, declared width and height or aspect ratio, meaningful alt text, and the policy's visible attribution.
The image frame reserves space before loading. A missing image preserves that sunken frame and readable alt text, never a spinner, jump, raw URL or invisible element.
The component imports only the local manifest and approved strings. It does not fetch, calculate coordinates, derive orientation, initialize a map, add a control, or import client JavaScript.
The image and caption expose no technical token, raw degree, secret, provider template or unapproved copy; attribution stays visible and legible in both themes.
steps.scenario_name: El surfista ve el break y hacia dónde mira sin abrir otro mapa
steps.u8_observation: El mapa se siente parte de la ficha de mi playa, no una página cargando encima. Veo dónde está el break y la flecha de orientación sin una leyenda complicada, y si no hay señal queda un cuadro tranquilo que todavía explica qué debería estar ahí.
steps.implementation_notes: Move the existing unshipped .img-frame recipe from src/styles/recipes.css into components.css with the component markup. The credit may be a static caption or approved link; if it is a link it must meet the existing 44 px target rule. The map never receives a browser-side loading state: native image failure plus the reserved frame is the settled offline/degrade surface.

steps.name: Spot-page mount and map cache strategy integrate serially
criteria: The static map appears once on the Spanish spot page, never home, tomorrow, report or archive; SpotDetail retains both day summaries and its report action.
The emitted image has loading=lazy and the map adds zero document bytes or route JavaScript; page-weight output still reports the spot document under its 14 KB ceiling.
When the owner worker is available, map assets use its cache-first bounded-image policy. An uncached offline image leaves a usable reserved alt-text frame with no request loop.
The source, attribution and generated asset identity stay paired in the emitted page; a manifest mismatch refuses the build instead of crediting one image while showing another.
steps.scenario_name: El mapa de la playa carga tarde sin pesar ni romper la página
steps.u8_observation: La página sigue ligera. El mapa aparece cuando llego a él y no tapa la llamada ni el botón de reportar; sin señal, su espacio no salta ni se convierte en un error técnico.
steps.implementation_notes: SERIALIZED INTEGRATION: SpotDetail.astro is the shared host (X10 precedent) and public/sw.js is owned by F-WORKS-WITH-NO-SIGNAL, not present on this branch. X12 must land or grant a serialized cache edit before this step dispatches. Do not create a second service worker. The native reserved-frame degrade is required even before the cache owner lands; the 5 MB LRU rule is asserted only against the real worker when available.

steps.name: Built surface proves map source, orientation and honest offline state
criteria: The future run proves every eligible spot page has one lazy local WebP, policy attribution, correct asset identity and an orientation marker tied to its seed record.
A bad asset, absent cache and offline visit leave a fixed-size readable-alt frame without horizontal overflow, technical error, map fetch, tile request, map library or displaced report action.
The real build rejects a missing credit, mismatched manifest, over-target asset or unresolved map input before `dist/` is accepted; the page-weight and zero-route-JavaScript assertions remain green.
The map passes two-theme contrast, 390 px, reduced-motion, type, token and attribution legibility checks, plus a fresh source-blind U8 observation.
steps.scenario_name: El surfista encuentra su break sin abrir un mapa pesado
steps.u8_observation: Puedo reconocer el lugar y su orientación de un vistazo. No me aparece un mapa que lucha por cargar, no me saca de la página y aun sin señal queda claro qué mapa debía ver.
steps.implementation_notes: JIT DISTILL ONLY: do not author future feature files, steps, fixtures, expectation charter, tags or RED-classification evidence while mapping. When Slice-05 legally opens after X11, the host integration and the cache owner are available, add the six production-build and browser behaviors in slice-05-contract.md. The image/worker failure paths are concrete example cases; deterministic asset-policy laws use fast-check at the build boundary.
